reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: the licence grant is expressly 'non-exclusive' (p0030, p0043, p0049) and none of the cited paragraphs imposes a sole-supplier, requirements or no-third-party-procurement obligation on the Licensee (our party).
The redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no comment is attached, which is the expected output for a compliant finding — nothing is being raised as a negotiation issue.

The rationale correctly triages the other 'exclusive' hits: the Field of Use 'exclusive purpose' language and Article II restrictions are scope/anti-sublicensing limits, and the exclusive-jurisdiction and non-exclusive-remedy clauses do not create exclusive dealing.

Treating the Article XXII Right of First Refusal as out of scope for EXCLUSIVITY (a change-of-control/transfer constraint, better handled under the change-of-control rule) is consistent with the rule's procurement-exclusivity focus and with the no-double-flagging instruction.
Deterministic check ('no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains') passes, corroborating the compliance conclusion.
